author: BBC News
description:
At least 30 people have been killed in a Russian glide bomb attack on two civilian buses in the eastern front line city of Kramatorsk, rescue officials said. 

Authorities said three people were also killed in the village of Bilenke, part of the Kramatorsk community. Another 18 people were wounded, said Donetsk regional head Vadym Filashkin, accusing Russia of targeting buses carrying passengers to kill as many civilians as possible. 

Kramatorsk and neighbouring Slovyansk are part of a so-called fortress belt that Moscow is trying to seize as part of Russian President Vladimir Putin's claim to the entire Ukrainian industrial region of Donbas. 

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said: "This strike will not go without our response."

Reeta Chakrabarti presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Dan Johnson.

What began as a revolt over public school funding has spilled into a much bigger fight over the future of France.
 
Now, hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets, and clashes with police have left teenagers and officers injured. More than 6,000 people have been arrested, most of them minors.
 
But what sparked these demonstrations? How could they shape next year’s election in France? And why have they become a conservative political talking point in the US?
 
The Global Story’s own Tristan Redman — a Paris resident himself — speaks with co-host Asma Khalid about the history of Parisian street protests, what he’s heard from students on the ground, and what this movement could mean for France’s future.

author: BBC News
description:
Gears of War, one of the video games that helped Microsoft's Xbox to win over millions of fans, is back.
 
Prequel E-Day takes players back to where it all started, telling the origin story of humanity's conflict with The Locust - the series' horrifying enemy species.
 
The game's been well-received by critics and players, but it's also seen as a big test of Xbox's new direction.
 
Unlike recent flagship titles from the company's studios, which have been released on PlayStation 5 and, in some cases, Nintendo Switch, E-Day is being pushed as an Xbox exclusive.
 
The apparent goal is to draw players back to the brand, but critics have questioned whether that's realistic at a time when console prices are higher than ever.
 
BBC Newsbeat's Tom Richardson spoke to developer The Coalition - the makers of E-Day - about what staying exclusive means to them.

description:
More than 1,400 people in Gaza have been killed in Israeli attacks since the start of the ceasefire on 10 October last year, according to Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
 
The ceasefire saw thousands of Palestinians held by Israel released in return for the remaining hostages held in Gaza, and an agreement to end the war - which was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 taken hostage.
 
But even during the ceasefire, Israel has continued launching strikes in Gaza almost every day.
 
Israel says it is targeting Hamas operatives and accuses Hamas of continued violations of the ceasefire.
 
The total death toll from Israeli attacks since the start of the war in Gaza now stands at more than 74,000, according to the Gaza health ministry.

Over 10 years since the EU referendum that saw the UK vote to leave the European Union, French finance minister Roland Lescure has invited Britain to "come all the way" back to the EU.
 
Hi comments come after UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham signalled a second Brexit referendum was "possible" in a future Labour election manifesto.
 
When asked about Burnham's comments, Lescure told the BBC: "British people decided, and that's obviously their 100% right, and if they're willing to come back, they will have to decide."
 
"But what I can tell them is: come back, anytime," he added.

author: BBC News
description:
A judge in the US state of Tennessee has ruled officials must preserve all evidence related to the failed execution of Christa Pike. 
 
Judge Myles ordered that "anything that was in the actual room needs to be preserved and maintained," including IV lines and syringes, as well as waste, like packaging, inserts, and labels.
 
She also advised the state to take "special care" not to misplace or accidentally delete any information that may be pertinent to the case.
 
Pike, who was sentenced to death after murdering Colleen Slemmer with her then-boyfriend in 1995, survived two lethal injections on 30 September.
 
Her Lawyer Randy Spivey says he was told Pike was brain dead on Monday, and it was expected that she would have her life support machine turned off on Tuesday, but instead she woke up and began speaking.
 
Pike remains in hospital, where she is receiving critical medical care and is being restrained at her hands and feet.
 
Subscribe to our channel here: https://bbc.in/bbcnews
title: Judge orders botched execution evidence to be preserved | BBC News

author: BBC News
description:
An elderly woman whose eviction sparked nationwide protests over Spain's housing crisis and a political row that triggered early elections has died, according to Madrid's tenants union.
 
Maricarmen Abascal, 87, was forcibly removed on a stretcher from her apartment of more than 70 years on 23 September after she was unable to afford steep rent increases.
 
The company that owned the flat later offered to allow her to return at a lower rate - but she was unable to sign an agreement as she had been admitted to hospital.
 
Announcing her death, Madrid Tenants' Union said Abascal's situation marked "a turning point in the history of this country".

author: BBC News
description:
Following an emergency court hearing on Wednesday, Christa Pike’s lawyers said preserving evidence from her failed execution was just the first step in a long legal battle after the 50-year-old death row inmate survived an execution attempt last week.

The judge ordered the state to preserve a broad range of physical evidence such as IVs and syringes – as well as all communications and surveillance video.
 
Her lawyers said it was necessary for transparency – and that the public should not simply take the state’s word about what happened.
 
The night before Pike woke up and began speaking, her lawyers said they believed she was brain dead and were told life support would be removed the next day.
 
She woke up "angry and confused", they said, asking "where am I?".
 
Her recovery, they added, will be a long road. It’s unclear if she’ll regain function of her arms which they say are extremely swollen.
